what_happened: The job was meant to add an in-flight table. The table is written at stage changes and read when the drain starts. It was rejected at the final verdict with one major finding and no unmet criteria or failed checks listed. In the real drain, the table records the wrong work tree. RealSteps::worktree (drain.rs:1856-1858) returns the kept-work directory used for timed-out jobs, not the producer's live work tree. The table would therefore point a restarted drain at the wrong directory.
cause: The in-flight table's correctness depends on the real implementation (RealSteps) returning the right path. Tests probably used a fake steps object that supplies the path directly, so nothing exercised the real accessor. Criteria and checks only show that the table is written and read, not that its recorded work tree is the producer's live one. Two similarly named directories (kept-work and live work tree) invite confusion, and only the verifier's read of the diff at the final verdict compares them, where rejection is the only outcome. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the plan or tests.
prevention: Add a test for any recorded-state feature that runs through the real implementation (RealSteps) instead of a fake. It would start a producer stage, read the in-flight table entry, and assert that the recorded path equals the directory the producer is actually working in. It would cover both the normal case and the timed-out, kept-work case. The reading's criterion should name this real-versus-recorded comparison, so the check runs before the final verdict.
proposed_request:
Fix the in-flight table so that, in the real drain, the work tree it records for a running job is the producer's live work tree, not the kept-work directory used for timed-out jobs. The fault is in RealSteps::worktree in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. Acceptance:
- A test using the real steps implementation, not a fake, starts a producer stage and shows the table entry's work tree equals the directory the producer is working in.
- A test shows a timed-out job whose work is kept still records its live work tree while it runs, and only uses the kept-work directory after the timeout.
- The drain start-up read of the table still passes its existing tests.
- Changes are limited to drain.rs and its tests, plus a changelog entry.
